title: #CULT
dek: Vishwak Sen attempts a bold survival thriller, but the violence overwhelms the suspense.
review: Vishwak Sen's #CULT begins with an interesting premise. A lavish Goa party turns into a deadly survival game. It's the kind of setup that should keep audiences guessing until the final minute.
The film has visual ambition, but the screenplay takes too long to establish real tension. The opening stretches its setup without giving us characters worth investing in.
Vishwak Sen brings intensity and screen presence. His action sequences work, but the writing doesn't give his character enough depth.
The biggest weakness is the excessive violence. Each new killing attempts to shock, yet the repetition gradually reduces its impact. Suspense needs uncertainty, not simply more blood.
The mystery initially raises interesting questions, but the eventual revelations follow familiar revenge-drama territory.
Ravi Basrur's background score, cinematography and production design give the film a strong atmosphere. Unfortunately, technical quality cannot compensate for weak storytelling.
MovieHmm Verdict: #CULT is an ambitious genre experiment that needed stronger characters, smarter survival challenges and a tighter screenplay.
works: Vishwak Sen's screen presence, ambitious slasher concept, Ravi Basrur's background score, action and production design.
misses: Repetitive graphic violence, weak suspense, slow opening, underdeveloped characters and predictable revelations.
